data.title: Criminal Psychology Research
data.text: Exploring the causes, characteristics, and intervention strategies of criminal psychology to support crime prevention and rehabilitation.

data.title: Overview of Criminal Psychology
data.text: This chapter introduces the definition, history, basic theories, and research fields of criminal psychology.

items.title: Definition of Criminal Psychology
items.text: Criminal psychology is the discipline that studies criminal behavior and its psychological mechanisms, aiming to understand offenders' psychological characteristics and behavioral motivations.

items.title: Development History of Criminal Psychology
items.text: Criminal psychology originated in the late 19th century and gradually became an independent discipline alongside the development of psychology and law.

items.title: Main Research Fields
items.text: These include the causes of criminal psychology, crime type analysis, and criminal psychology assessment and intervention.

items.title: Relationship with Other Disciplines
items.text: Criminal psychology is closely related to law, sociology, biology, and other disciplines, jointly exploring criminal phenomena.

items.title: Biological Theories
items.text: Examines the influence of factors such as genetics and neurophysiology on criminal behavior.

items.title: Psychological Theories
items.text: Analyzes the links between psychological factors such as personality, cognition, and emotion and criminal behavior.

items.title: Sociological Theories
items.text: Studies how social environments and cultural backgrounds shape criminal psychology.

items.title: Comprehensive Theories
items.text: Combines biological, psychological, and sociological perspectives to comprehensively explain criminal psychology.

data.title: Formation of Criminal Psychology
data.text: This chapter explores the influence of individual factors, environmental factors, and psychological processes on criminal psychology.

items.title: Genetic Factors
items.text: Investigates the potential link between genes and criminal behavior.

items.title: Psychological Traits
items.text: Examines the relationship between personality traits such as aggressiveness and impulsivity and crime.

items.title: Personality Disorders
items.text: Analyzes how mental illnesses such as antisocial personality disorder drive criminal behavior.

items.title: Early Experiences
items.text: Studies the long-term effects of childhood trauma and domestic violence on criminal psychology.

items.title: Family Environment
items.text: Examines how family structure and parenting styles shape criminal psychology.

items.title: Social Environment Influence
items.text: Analyzes the inducing effects of peer pressure and community environment on criminal behavior.

items.title: Economic Factors
items.text: Studies the relationship between economic problems such as poverty and unemployment and crime rates.

items.title: Cultural Background
items.text: Examines the influence of cultural values on criminal psychology.

items.title: Cognitive Processes
items.text: Analyzes offenders' thinking patterns and decision-making models and their impact on behavior.

items.title: Emotional Processes
items.text: Examines the relationship between emotion regulation, emotional deficit, and criminal behavior.

items.title: Behavioral Motivations
items.text: Investigates offenders' internal motivations, such as profit-driven motives and a desire for revenge.

items.title: Decision-Making Mechanisms
items.text: Analyzes the decision-making process and psychological mechanisms of offenders before committing a crime.

data.title: Crime Types and Psychological Characteristics
data.text: This chapter analyzes the psychological characteristics of violent crime, property crime, and cybercrime.

items.title: Psychological Characteristics of Murder
items.text: Examines the psychological motivations of murderers, such as emotional conflict and disputes over interests.

items.title: Psychological Characteristics of Robbery
items.text: Analyzes robbers' risk-taking psychology and dependence on violence.

items.title: Psychological Characteristics of Sex Crimes
items.text: Studies the psychological distortion and behavioral patterns of sex offenders.

items.title: Psychological Characteristics of Domestic Violence
items.text: Examines the desire for control and emotional deficits of domestic violence perpetrators.

items.title: Psychological Characteristics of Theft
items.text: Analyzes thieves' mentality of getting away with it and their desire for material goods.

items.title: Psychological Characteristics of Fraud
items.text: Examines fraudsters' deception techniques and psychological manipulation abilities.

items.title: Psychological Characteristics of Corruption
items.text: Studies corrupt officials' lust for power and moral degradation.

items.title: Psychological Characteristics of Money Laundering
items.text: Analyzes money launderers' risk-aversion psychology and legal-avoidance strategies.

items.title: Psychological Characteristics of Hackers
items.text: Examines hackers' worship of technology and psychology of challenging authority.

items.title: Psychological Characteristics of Online Fraud
items.text: Analyzes online fraudsters' ability to disguise themselves and psychological manipulation techniques.

items.title: Psychological Characteristics of Cyber Violence
items.text: Studies the anonymity psychology and aggressiveness of cyber violence perpetrators.

items.title: Internet Addiction and Crime
items.text: Examines internet addicts' dependence on the virtual world and its association with criminal behavior.

data.title: Criminal Psychology Assessment and Intervention
data.text: This chapter introduces criminal psychology assessment methods and intervention strategies, and explores preventive measures.

items.title: Psychological Testing
items.text: Assesses offenders' psychological states and personality traits through standardized tests.

items.title: Behavioral Observation
items.text: Observes offenders' daily behavior to analyze their behavioral patterns and psychological motivations.

items.title: Interview Techniques
items.text: Understands offenders' psychological journey and criminal motivations through in-depth interviews.

items.title: Case Analysis
items.text: Analyzes offenders' psychological characteristics and behavioral patterns through representative cases.

items.title: Psychotherapy
items.text: Helps offenders correct psychological problems through psychological counseling and therapy.

items.title: Behavior Modification
items.text: Helps offenders change unhealthy behavioral patterns through behavioral training.

items.title: Social Support
items.text: Provides social resource support to help offenders reintegrate into society.

items.title: Legal Intervention
items.text: Constrains and punishes criminal behavior through legal means.

items.title: Early Intervention
items.text: Prevents behavioral problems in potential offenders through early psychological intervention.

items.title: Educational Prevention
items.text: Improves the public's legal awareness and mental health through education.

items.title: Community Prevention
items.text: Enhances social cohesion and reduces crime triggers through community activities.

items.title: Policy-Based Prevention
items.text: Reduces social inequality and lowers crime rates through policy making.

data.title: Applications of Criminal Psychology
data.text: This chapter explores the applications of criminal psychology in criminal justice, crime prevention, and research and education.

items.title: Criminal Psychological Profiling
items.text: Depicts offender characteristics through psychological analysis to assist in solving cases.

items.title: Interrogation Techniques
items.text: Uses psychological methods to improve interrogation efficiency and obtain truthful confessions.

items.title: Witness Psychology
items.text: Studies witnesses' psychological states and their impact on testimony credibility.

items.title: Jury Decision-Making
items.text: Analyzes jurors' psychological processes and their impact on verdicts.

items.title: Crime Prevention Strategies
items.text: Prevents criminal behavior through psychological intervention and social support.

items.title: Prison Psychological Rehabilitation
items.text: Helps inmates correct psychological problems through psychotherapy to reduce recidivism.

items.title: Community Correction
items.text: Helps offenders reintegrate into society and reduce recidivism risk through community support.

items.title: Recidivism Prevention
items.text: Reduces the likelihood of reoffending through psychological assessment and intervention.

items.title: Criminal Psychology Research
items.text: Deepens the understanding of criminal psychology through scientific research and advances the discipline.

items.title: Criminal Psychology Education
items.text: Cultivates professionals through education to raise the level of criminal psychology application.

items.title: Professional Training
items.text: Enhances justice personnel's psychological knowledge and skills through training.

items.title: Academic Exchange
items.text: Promotes international cooperation and development in criminal psychology through academic exchange.

data.title: Future Development Trends
data.text: This chapter explores the future directions of criminal psychology in technology application, interdisciplinary cooperation, and ethical challenges.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and Criminal Psychology
items.text: Uses AI technology to analyze crime data and improve crime prediction capabilities.

items.title: Big Data Analysis
items.text: Mines the patterns and psychological characteristics of criminal behavior through big data technology.

items.title: Virtual Reality Technology
items.text: Uses VR technology to simulate crime scenes and study offenders' psychological responses.

items.title: Neuroscience Research
items.text: Explores the biological basis of criminal behavior through neuroscience research.

items.title: Psychology and Law
items.text: Strengthens cooperation between psychology and law to make the justice system more scientific.

items.title: Psychology and Medicine
items.text: Deepens the understanding of criminal psychology by combining psychology and medicine.

items.title: Psychology and Sociology
items.text: Comprehensively analyzes criminal phenomena through cross-disciplinary research in psychology and sociology.

items.title: Psychology and Information Technology
items.text: Combines psychology and information technology to develop new tools for crime prevention and intervention.

items.title: Ethical Issues
items.text: Examines the ethical dilemmas in criminal psychology research and their solutions.

items.title: Privacy Protection
items.text: Studies how to protect personal privacy in the application of criminal psychology.

items.title: Data Security
items.text: Analyzes the security risks of criminal psychology data and protective measures.

items.title: Future Challenges
items.text: Examines the technical and social challenges criminal psychology may face in its future development.
